authorial_core.baseline_prompt_en: An environmental photograph of an ominous rural encounter, an encounter with a shared village taboo. The principal subject is a woman guided by the supplied face and hair appearance; portray her as a fictional adult archivist. Use the supplied image as the face and hair appearance reference. Her face has softly rounded contours and dark eyes; her hair is a short dark bob with a light separated fringe. In a Korean hillside village at pale early dawn, she has stopped beside a communal stone well. Its low circular rim and entire heavy wooden lid are visible, the lid closed and dry. A fresh trail of wet bare footprints starts on the dry earth immediately beside the well lid and leads outward toward her boots, dark individual soles becoming faint farther along the lane. Her face is in readable three-quarter view, chin slightly lowered, eyes directed along that trail. She stands with both boots planted apart, torso turned toward the well, both hands supporting a small closed field notebook at her waist. The unfinished purpose of her visit is readable in the notebook and her arrested attention. Two adult residents remain within separate open house doorways behind the well, their bodies held back by the thresholds, faces and eyes turned toward the same wet trail. One has a hand resting on the door frame. Their reluctance leaves a clear empty band of ground around the well. Worn tiled roofs, rough plaster and a narrow packed-earth lane give the scene a lived-in scale. A simple charcoal work jacket and softly rumpled pale shirt frame the archivist's face; her quiet, concentrated presence is compelling within the uneasy distance between people. Frame her full length near the right edge, keeping the entire well lid and the complete visible route from its first footprint to her boots in the lower center. Eye-level naturalistic 35 mm photography with enough depth of field to read the residents, cool dawn light, tactile damp earth and restrained muted color.
